subject: Initiate latency circuit-breaker & fallback for model omega-prime (p95 regression)
body:
From: Helen Kim <helen.kim@orionfinance.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: ops@orionfinance.com
Date: Mon, 09 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase after today's omega-prime rollout

Hi Jonas,

We started seeing a sharp p95 jump on requests routed to model: omega-prime v3.2 after the 03:00 UTC rollout this morning. Baseline p95 has historically been ~420-480ms for our traffic profile; since 08:30 PDT this morning p95 is at ~1.6s and impacting user-facing latency for autocomplete and document previews.

Attached is a p95 trace and a small sample of spans showing tails around long prompt lengths. We are in the middle of a high-traffic window (end-of-quarter batch jobs + product sync) and this is materially affecting UX. Our contract has a 600ms p95 commitment for the endpoints in scope (see SLA section in the SOW).

Can Redwood temporarily route our traffic to the previous stable variant (omega-stable-v2) or apply any mitigation while you investigate? Our preference is minimal change on our side, but we need p95 back under the contractual threshold ASAP.

Thanks,
Helen Kim
Head of Platform Reliability
Orion Finance

Attachments: p95_trace_2028-10-09.png, hourly-spans-20281009.json

---

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Helen Kim <helen.kim@orionfinance.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Oct 2028 10:15:12 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase after today's omega-prime rollout

Thanks for the heads up, Helen — very sorry for the disruption. We’ve already pulled the live telemetry and see the same p95 drift in our global dashboards (not limited to any single region).

Proposed immediate mitigation (operational ask):
- Activate latency circuit-breaker for Orion Finance traffic: route 60% of eligible requests to omega-stable-v2, retain 40% on omega-prime v3.2 for monitoring (canary).
- Apply a soft traffic cap to long-sequence requests (>1024 tokens) for 24 hours.
- Flush any KV prefix cache for the affected model variant across the dedicated pool (low risk).

This will be a live traffic switch but should be reversible within 15 minutes. We expect p95 to drop back under SLA (~520ms estimated) after the fallback.

Operational approvals needed: product/SRE sign-off (Marissa, Rishi) and account alignment (Lauren). Also note we’ll need a formal temporary SLA carveout request for any time window where latency exceeds the contract threshold; I’ll kick that off with legal if we proceed.

If everyone agrees I’ll send a one-line confirmation to OPS and execute with infra; target start in 20 minutes to minimize customer impact.

Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Oct 2028 10:40:05 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase after today's omega-prime rollout

Jonas — quick technical readout:
- Root cause hypothesis: a kernel path introduced in v3.2 increases per-token overhead for prompt distributions with dense metadata (we're seeing larger attention matrices on ~8% of Orion's requests).
- Risk of full rollback: low for correctness; model weights unchanged, only execution path differs. The KV cache flush is advisable because the cache population for the new kernel mixes prefixes in-memory differently and could prolong degradation post-switch.

Operational plan I support:
1) Circuit-breaker to omega-stable-v2 at 60% split with canary telemetry.
2) Flush KV cache for the omega-prime instances servicing ORF namespace.
3) Run a 30-minute validation window on telemetry (latency/p95 and error-rate) before deciding to fully cutover or rollforward a patch.

I can be on standby during the switch and own the validation dashboard.

— Rishi
Senior Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Oct 2028 11:05:33 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase after today's omega-prime rollout

+1 from SRE operations. Quick notes:
- I’ll open JIRA-OPS-4742 and tag infra on the KV flush and routing change.
- Estimated impact window: ~20–40 minutes for the change to converge globally; no expected service downtime.
- Post-switch expectation: p95 target ~<= 550ms within 10–15 minutes; we will monitor error budget burn.

Action items for execution if Jonas triggers:
- Infra: apply routing delta (60/40) + enforce long-seq cap; confirm KV flush completed.
- Rishi: sign off on the 30-minute validation window.
- Lauren: confirm we have customer permission for a temporary fallback and to log a SLA exception (we should get an email OK from Orion).

I’ll stand up the incident channel and push metrics to the shared board.

Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Production
Redwood Inference

---

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Helen Kim <helen.kim@orionfinance.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Oct 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Action plan: activate circuit-breaker + fallback to omega-stable-v2 (now)

Hi Helen — thanks again for flagging this. Short summary and next steps: 

What we’re doing now
- Activate latency circuit-breaker for Orion Finance traffic immediately: 60% -> omega-stable-v2, 40% remains on omega-prime v3.2 for telemetry.
- Apply token-length cap for long requests (>1024 tokens) for 24 hours.
- Flush KV/prefix cache for omega-prime instances in your tenant pool.
- Opened JIRA-OPS-4742 to track infra work and verification.

Why this approach
- Safest path to restore p95 quickly while retaining a canary for validation. Rishi and Marissa have validated operational steps.

Expected outcome
- We expect p95 to return to ~520ms (below contractual threshold) within 15 minutes of the switch. We will monitor for 30 minutes of stable telemetry before considering a full cutover.

SLA carveout / formal note
- Because your contract calls out a 600ms p95 commitment, we will log this as a temporary SLA exception window while remediation proceeds. For our records and for your legal/procurement teams, please reply to this email with explicit approval for the fallback ("I approve the temporary fallback to omega-stable-v2 and the associated SLA exception window"). Lauren / Ben — please prepare the formal carveout note for our SLA tracker and legal.

If you’re good, I’ll execute the switch now and confirm back in the thread with telemetry.

Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: monthly-usage-Oct-2028.csv
